run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: The alert is for workload/org clientorg-alpha, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, cluster us-prod-eks, but nothing with that identity exists in the two indices or in the connected cluster. app-235-change-history holds exactly 4 documents, all ci-cd-cluster changes (gitlab-runner scale 2→3 on v16.7.0 at 2026-11-23T15:57:59Z, argocd-server v2.9.2→v2.9.3 at 12:57:59Z, jenkins 2.426.2-lts→2.426.3-lts at 11:57:59Z, flux-controller config-update on 2026-11-16), and app-235-cluster-inventory holds documents for the same ci/cd namespaces only (gitlab-runner, jenkins, argocd-server, tekton-pipelines, flux-controller, all status Running). The connected Kubernetes cluster is a kind cluster with namespaces default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo — no clientorg-alpha namespace, no lambda-dashboard-monitoring deployment, and all 32 pods are Running with restartCount 0. Prometheus and Jaeger queries all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no metric, error-rate or trace evidence could be read for any service. On the available evidence the premise 'the alert started right after a deployment' is not supported for the alerting workload: the only recent recorded change is an unrelated ci-cd-cluster gitlab-runner scale-up with an unchanged version, and the alert itself describes a gradual 8-hour decline rather than a step change. The root cause of the onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease alert cannot be established from these sources; the otel-demo feature-flag set is a checked-and-clean item (all fault flags default off) that shows no fault injection here.

No inventory entry matches lambda-dashboard-monitoring or a clientorg-alpha namespace.

The connected Kubernetes cluster has exactly the namespaces default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; there is no namespace named clientorg-alpha.

The connected cluster runs 24 Deployments, all in kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo (e.g. otel-demo ad/cart/checkout/currency/email/frontend/payment etc. on ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-*, plus prometheus, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, flagd); no Deployment named lambda-dashboard-monitoring or in a clientorg-alpha namespace exists.

All 32 pods in the connected cluster report phase Running with restartCount 0 and start times of 2026-11-23T14:36–14:38Z, so no pod in this cluster shows a crash, restart or Evicted/OOMKilled condition at query time.

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap defines fault flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) and every one of them has defaultVariant 'off', i.e. no fault is switched on in the declared configuration.

The alerting rules loaded in the otel-demo prometheus ConfigMap are CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (checkout CheckoutService/PlaceOrder server-span error ratio > 0.5), OpsPilotAgentAbsent and OpsPilotModelCallsFailing; there is no rule producing onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease or referencing lambda-dashboard-monitoring/clientorg-alpha, so the P1 alert does not originate from this Prometheus instance.

The prometheus-server container in pod prometheus-9bc78b7f7-k84v7 is running and writing log lines throughout 17:38–17:57Z (repeated 'Error on ingesting out-of-order exemplars' warnings), so the pod itself is alive even though the Prometheus query path used by the tools returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the gitlab-runner scale 2→3 recorded at 2026-11-23T15:57:59Z. It targets cluster ci-cd / namespace ci, not the alerting cluster us-prod-eks or workload clientorg-alpha; it is a replica-count scale with an unchanged version (v16.7.0→v16.7.0, image gitlab/gitlab-runner:v16.7.0 still reported Running with 3 replicas); and it precedes the ~17:28Z alert onset by about 90 minutes while the alert describes a gradual decrease over 8 hours (~09:28Z onward). No evidence ties it to an online-devices signal.

Rejected for this alert: a fault injected through the otel-demo flagd feature flags. All declared fault flags are 'off' by default and the otel-demo pods are Running with 0 restarts; no evidence connects the otel-demo workloads to the clientorg-alpha online-devices alert.

The deployment the alert is said to follow happened in cluster us-prod-eks for app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, which is outside every reachable source here: the two indices record only the ci-cd cluster and the connected Kubernetes API is a kind cluster with otel-demo/kube-system workloads. The cause of the online-devices decline would therefore have to be retrieved from that cluster's own change history and metrics.

Because the alert describes a gradual 8-hour decline (~56% for over 30m) rather than a step change, a single deployment minutes before onset is a weak candidate; other candidates not yet excluded are a slow leak/backlog or a gradual capacity change starting around 2026-11-23T09:28Z, none of which can be tested here without the us-prod-eks metrics.

Nothing in the connected environment shows an unhealthy workload: all 32 pods are Running with restartCount 0, and no Kubernetes Events were returned for the window. This is consistent with the alerting subject being outside this environment rather than with a visible outage here.

Pull the change record and metrics for cluster us-prod-eks / lambda-dashboard-monitoring (the deployment timeline around 2026-11-23T15:57–17:28Z and the onlineDevices series from ~09:28Z) from that cluster's own change-history and monitoring integration, since none of it is present in app-235-change-history or app-235-cluster-inventory.

Restore the Prometheus and Jaeger query path used by the tooling (every metric, label, rule and trace query returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE even though pods prometheus-9bc78b7f7-k84v7, prometheus-readonly-proxy-7567c75596-nwrxw and jaeger-698d849b7b-qhlhm are Running) so that error-rate and latency signals can be read before drawing any conclusion about service impact.

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.
view.incomplete_reason: limit: the newest 40 of 119 matching lines are shown

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

content.alerting_rules_yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
